nodes.name: U.S. Constitution
nodes.dm: Amended by 2/3 of Congress + 3/4 of states; meaning fixed by the Supreme Court
nodes.description: Supreme law. Allocates power among three branches and the states; the Bill of Rights limits all of them.

nodes.name: Voters / electorate
nodes.description: Ultimate source of political legitimacy. Power is exercised only at intervals, through districts and the Electoral College, and is heavily mediated by parties, money and media.

nodes.name: Consumers / households
nodes.description: Spending, borrowing and attention are the raw material every business and platform competes for. Diffuse, rarely coordinated.

nodes.name: Workforce / labor
nodes.description: Labor power exercised through strikes, quits and union bargaining; mostly unorganized.

nodes.name: Civil society & protest movements
nodes.dm: No single leader; ACLU, faith coalitions, No Kings network, local organizers
nodes.description: Street power, litigation, boycotts and mutual aid. Sets limits on what governments can do without visible resistance.

nodes.name: Juries & grand juries
nodes.description: Only citizen body that can convict, acquit or refuse to indict. A hard check on prosecutors and, at times, on the executive.

nodes.name: Federal civil service
nodes.dm: ~2.1M civilian employees after 2025 reductions; AFGE bargaining rights stripped by EO in 2025
nodes.description: Institutional memory and day-to-day execution of federal law. Its independence was the target of Schedule F / Policy-Career reclassification and mass RIFs.

nodes.name: President of the United States
nodes.dm: Donald J. Trump (47th president, second term)
nodes.description: Commander in chief, head of the executive branch, party leader. Post-2024 the office claims broad removal power over agency heads and has used emergency statutes (IEEPA tariffs, Title 10 Guard deployments) aggressively.

nodes.name: Vice President
nodes.description: President of the Senate (tie-breaking votes), first in line of succession, and a political heir with his own donor network.

nodes.name: White House Office
nodes.dm: Chief of Staff Susie Wiles; Deputy CoS Stephen Miller (immigration/policy)
nodes.description: Gatekeeper to the president. Sets personnel, coordinates agencies, controls the press pool and immigration enforcement targets.

nodes.name: Office of Management & Budget
nodes.description: Writes the budget, reviews every major regulation (OIRA), and has used impoundment, rescissions and grant freezes to override congressional spending.

nodes.name: National Security Council
nodes.dm: Marco Rubio (acting national security advisor, concurrently Secretary of State)
nodes.description: Coordinates defense, intelligence and diplomacy for the president.

nodes.name: U.S. Trade Representative
nodes.description: Negotiates trade deals and administers tariff actions; the operational arm of the 2025–26 tariff regime.

nodes.name: Department of Justice
nodes.dm: Attorney General Pam Bondi; Deputy AG Todd Blanche
nodes.description: Federal prosecution, antitrust, civil rights, and litigation defense of the executive. Traditional independence norms weakened after 2025.

nodes.name: FBI
nodes.dm: Director Kash Patel; Deputy Director Dan Bongino
nodes.description: Principal federal investigative and domestic intelligence agency; ~38,000 employees.

nodes.name: DEA
nodes.description: Drug enforcement, scheduling input, and a large overseas footprint.

nodes.name: ATF
nodes.description: Firearms, explosives and arson enforcement; licensing of gun dealers.

nodes.name: U.S. Marshals Service
nodes.description: Executes federal court orders, fugitive apprehension, witness protection. An executive agency that enforces judicial rulings.

nodes.name: Bureau of Prisons
nodes.description: ~155,000 federal inmates; 120+ facilities.

nodes.name: U.S. Attorneys (93 districts)
nodes.dm: Presidential appointees; several interim/acting after 2025 court challenges
nodes.description: Decide who gets charged federally. Charging discretion is one of the most concentrated forms of coercive power.

nodes.name: Solicitor General
nodes.description: Argues for the executive at the Supreme Court; heavy use of the emergency docket since 2025.

nodes.name: Department of Defense (Dept. of War)
nodes.description: ~1.3M active-duty, ~750k civilians, ~$900B+ budget. The largest organization of organized force on earth; also the largest customer of U.S. industry.

nodes.name: Joint Chiefs of Staff
nodes.description: Senior uniformed advisers; not in the operational chain of command but decisive in practice.

nodes.name: U.S. Army
nodes.dm: Secretary Dan Driscoll; Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George
nodes.description: ~450k active; Army Corps of Engineers sits here administratively.

nodes.name: U.S. Navy
nodes.dm: Secretary John Phelan; CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle
nodes.description: Sea control, nuclear triad (SSBNs), power projection.

nodes.name: U.S. Air Force
nodes.dm: Secretary Troy Meink; Chief of Staff Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach
nodes.description: Air superiority, ICBMs, bombers, airlift.

nodes.name: U.S. Marine Corps
nodes.description: Expeditionary force; used domestically in 2025 (Los Angeles).

nodes.name: U.S. Space Force
nodes.dm: Chief of Space Operations Gen. Chance Saltzman
nodes.description: Satellites, launch, missile warning; dependent on commercial launch.

nodes.name: National Security Agency
nodes.dm: Director (acting) after 2025 removal of Gen. Timothy Haugh
nodes.description: Signals intelligence and cyber; compelled cooperation from telecoms and platforms under FISA 702.

nodes.name: CIA
nodes.description: Human intelligence and covert action; briefs the president daily.

nodes.name: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
nodes.description: Nominal head of the 18-agency intelligence community; controls classification and intelligence sharing.

nodes.name: Department of Homeland Security
nodes.dm: Secretary Kristi Noem; ~$170B+ after 2025 reconciliation funding
nodes.description: Immigration enforcement, borders, Secret Service, Coast Guard, FEMA, cyber. The fastest-growing coercive budget in government.

nodes.name: ICE
nodes.dm: Acting Director Todd Lyons; targets set by Stephen Miller (White House)
nodes.description: Interior immigration enforcement and detention (~60k+ detained); hiring surge funded in 2025.

nodes.name: Customs & Border Protection
nodes.description: Border Patrol, ports of entry, and collection of tariffs; ~60k personnel.

nodes.name: U.S. Secret Service
nodes.description: Protective detail and financial-crimes investigations.

nodes.name: U.S. Coast Guard
nodes.description: Maritime law enforcement, ports, interdiction; a military service under DHS.

nodes.name: TSA
nodes.description: Screens ~2.5M passengers a day; sets no-fly and screening rules.

nodes.name: FEMA
nodes.description: Disaster grants and response; states depend on its money after storms and fires.

nodes.name: CISA
nodes.description: Cyber and infrastructure security; election-security role cut back in 2025.

nodes.name: USCIS
nodes.description: Adjudicates visas, green cards, citizenship; administers the $100k H-1B fee introduced in 2025.

nodes.name: Department of State
nodes.dm: Secretary Marco Rubio (USAID folded into State in 2025)
nodes.description: Diplomacy, sanctions policy input, visas (including student-visa revocations), foreign aid remnants.

nodes.name: Department of the Treasury
nodes.description: Issues the debt, collects taxes, runs sanctions, oversees banks (OCC), and holds the government's stakes in GSEs and, since 2025, in companies like Intel.

nodes.name: IRS
nodes.dm: CEO Frank Bisignano (also SSA Commissioner); staff cut ~25% in 2025
nodes.description: Collects ~$5T a year. Also decides tax-exempt status for universities, churches and nonprofits.

nodes.name: OFAC (sanctions)
nodes.description: Economic sanctions; can cut any bank, company or person out of the dollar system.

nodes.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
nodes.description: Charters and supervises national banks; lifted Wells Fargo's asset cap in 2025.

nodes.name: Department of the Interior
nodes.description: Manages ~500M acres, offshore leasing, tribal affairs, and energy permitting on public land.

nodes.name: Bureau of Land Management
nodes.description: 245M acres; grazing, mining and oil & gas leases.

nodes.name: National Park Service
nodes.description: 63 national parks and 430+ units; staffing cut in 2025.

nodes.name: Fish & Wildlife Service
nodes.description: Endangered Species Act listings and consultations that can stop projects.

nodes.name: Department of Agriculture
nodes.description: Farm subsidies, crop insurance, SNAP, forests, meat inspection; ~$200B+ budget.

nodes.name: U.S. Forest Service
nodes.description: 193M acres; timber, grazing, wildfire.

nodes.name: Food & Nutrition Service (SNAP/WIC)
nodes.description: SNAP reaches ~40M people; 2025 reconciliation law shifted costs to states and tightened work rules.

nodes.name: Department of Commerce
nodes.description: Export controls, CHIPS funding (incl. the government's Intel stake), census, patents, NOAA, tariff negotiations.

nodes.name: NOAA
nodes.description: Weather service, fisheries, climate data; staff cuts in 2025.

nodes.name: Census Bureau
nodes.description: Its counts apportion House seats and drive $2T+ in funding formulas; a 2025 push to exclude noncitizens is litigated.

nodes.name: Bureau of Industry & Security
nodes.description: Export controls on chips and tools; the chokepoint for Nvidia/AMD China sales.

nodes.name: Patent & Trademark Office
nodes.description: Grants the monopolies pharma and tech depend on.

nodes.name: Department of Labor
nodes.description: Wage and hour, pensions (ERISA), union reporting, jobs data (BLS commissioner fired 2025).

nodes.name: OSHA
nodes.description: Workplace safety inspections; roughly one inspector per 80,000 workers.

nodes.name: Department of Health & Human Services
nodes.description: ~$1.8T budget; Medicare, Medicaid, FDA, CDC, NIH. Reorganized and downsized in 2025 (MAHA agenda).
nodes.aliases: Department of Health and Human Services|HHS

nodes.name: FDA
nodes.description: Gatekeeper for drugs, devices, food and tobacco worth ~20% of consumer spending.

nodes.name: CDC
nodes.dm: Acting Director (after 2025 dismissal of Susan Monarez); vaccine advisory panel replaced
nodes.description: Public-health guidance and grants; authority contested with states after 2025.

nodes.name: NIH
nodes.description: ~$47B in research grants; leverage over universities via indirect-cost caps and terminations.

nodes.name: CMS (Medicare & Medicaid)
nodes.description: Pays ~$1.7T a year to hospitals, insurers and drugmakers; sets prices for the whole health economy.

nodes.name: Social Security Administration
nodes.description: ~$1.5T in benefits to ~70M people.

nodes.name: Department of Housing & Urban Development
nodes.description: Vouchers, public housing, community grants; conditions on funds used as leverage over cities.
nodes.aliases: Department of Housing and Urban Development

nodes.name: Department of Transportation
nodes.description: Highway money is the classic lever over states; FAA, NHTSA, FRA, transit grants.

nodes.name: FAA
nodes.description: Certifies aircraft, licenses launches, runs air traffic control.

nodes.name: Department of Energy
nodes.description: National labs, nuclear weapons complex (NNSA), LNG export approvals, grid emergency orders keeping plants open.

nodes.name: NNSA (nuclear weapons complex)
nodes.description: Builds and maintains the warheads.

nodes.name: Department of Education
nodes.dm: Secretary Linda McMahon; functions being transferred to other agencies
nodes.description: Student aid (~$1.6T loan portfolio), Title I, Title IX/civil-rights enforcement used as leverage over universities.

nodes.name: Department of Veterans Affairs
nodes.description: ~9M patients, ~480k employees, second-largest department.

nodes.name: EPA
nodes.description: Air, water, chemicals, vehicle rules; 2025 repeal of the greenhouse-gas endangerment finding and deep staff cuts.

nodes.name: Army Corps of Engineers
nodes.dm: Chief of Engineers Lt. Gen. William Graham
nodes.description: Wetlands permits, dams, ports, levees; civil works budget ~$8B.

nodes.name: Small Business Administration
nodes.description: Loan guarantees and disaster loans.

nodes.name: NASA
nodes.description: ~$25B; increasingly a customer of SpaceX rather than a builder.

nodes.name: Office of Personnel Management
nodes.description: Hiring rules, Schedule Policy/Career reclassification, RIF authority over the civil service.

nodes.name: General Services Administration
nodes.description: Federal buildings and procurement schedules; consolidated purchasing after 2025.

nodes.name: Federal Reserve
nodes.dm: Chair Kevin Warsh (since May 2026); Board of Governors; FOMC
nodes.description: Sets short-term interest rates, supervises the largest banks, and is lender of last resort. Its independence was tested by the 2025 attempt to remove Governor Lisa Cook.

nodes.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
nodes.description: Executes open-market operations and supervises Wall Street's biggest firms.

nodes.name: SEC
nodes.description: Disclosure, exchanges, asset managers, crypto (now permissive); enforcement retreat since 2025.

nodes.name: FTC
nodes.dm: Chair Andrew Ferguson (Democratic commissioners removed in 2025)
nodes.description: Antitrust and consumer protection; lost its Meta monopolization case in 2025, won a $2.5B Amazon Prime settlement.

nodes.name: FCC
nodes.description: Broadcast licenses, spectrum, mergers. Used license leverage over networks in 2025 (Kimmel suspension, Skydance conditions).

nodes.name: FDIC
nodes.description: Deposit insurance and resolution of failed banks.

nodes.name: CFPB
nodes.dm: Acting Director Russell Vought; staff largely dismissed
nodes.description: Consumer-finance regulator effectively dormant since 2025.

nodes.name: CFTC
nodes.description: Futures, swaps and, increasingly, crypto spot markets.

nodes.name: National Labor Relations Board
nodes.dm: Board members appointed after 2025 removals restored quorum; constitutionality under litigation
nodes.description: Certifies unions, adjudicates unfair labor practices.

nodes.name: Federal Election Commission
nodes.description: Campaign-finance disclosure and enforcement; largely inert.

nodes.name: EEOC
nodes.description: Employment discrimination; redirected toward DEI investigations in 2025.

nodes.name: FHFA
nodes.description: Conservator of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; also generated the criminal referrals used against Trump adversaries in 2025.

nodes.name: Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac
nodes.dm: CEOs Priscilla Almodovar / Diana Reid, under FHFA conservatorship; partial re-IPO under discussion
nodes.description: Guarantee ~$7T of mortgages; set the terms of American home finance.

nodes.name: U.S. Postal Service
nodes.description: ~630k employees; last-mile delivery for Amazon and mail-in ballots.

nodes.name: FERC
nodes.description: Interstate transmission, pipelines, wholesale power markets.

nodes.name: Nuclear Regulatory Commission
nodes.dm: Chairman David Wright; 2025 EO placed rules under OMB review
nodes.description: Licenses reactors; independence curtailed in 2025.

nodes.name: U.S. Congress
nodes.dm: 119th Congress; Republican majorities in both chambers
nodes.description: Writes the laws, holds the purse, confirms officials, can impeach. Power diminished in practice by delegation to the executive and by party discipline.

nodes.name: House of Representatives
nodes.dm: Speaker Mike Johnson; Majority Leader Steve Scalise; Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries
nodes.description: 435 members; originates revenue bills; impeachment.

nodes.name: U.S. Senate
nodes.dm: Majority Leader John Thune; Minority Leader Chuck Schumer; President pro tempore Chuck Grassley
nodes.description: 100 members; confirms judges and officials, ratifies treaties, tries impeachments; filibuster still intact.

nodes.name: House Rules Committee
nodes.description: Controls what reaches the House floor and on what terms; an arm of the Speaker.

nodes.name: House Appropriations
nodes.description: Writes the 12 spending bills.

nodes.name: Senate Appropriations
nodes.dm: Chair Susan Collins; Vice Chair Patty Murray
nodes.description: Senate side of the purse; the last venue where bipartisan bargaining is structurally required.

nodes.name: House Ways & Means
nodes.description: Taxes, tariffs, Social Security, Medicare.

nodes.name: Senate Finance
nodes.description: Taxes, trade, health entitlements.

nodes.name: House Judiciary
nodes.description: Courts, DOJ oversight, immigration law, impeachment articles.

nodes.name: Senate Judiciary
nodes.description: Judicial confirmations pipeline; blue-slip norm for district judges.

nodes.name: House Armed Services
nodes.description: Annual NDAA; prime contractors' favorite committee.

nodes.name: Senate Armed Services
nodes.description: NDAA and confirmation of generals and defense officials.

nodes.name: House Energy & Commerce
nodes.description: Health, telecom, energy, tech; widest jurisdiction in the House.

nodes.name: Senate Banking
nodes.description: Fed, banks, housing, crypto (GENIUS Act); confirmed Warsh 2026.

nodes.name: House Financial Services
nodes.description: Banks, SEC, crypto market-structure legislation.

nodes.name: House Oversight
nodes.description: Subpoena power over the whole executive; used selectively along party lines.

nodes.name: Senate Intelligence
nodes.dm: Chair Tom Cotton; Vice Chair Mark Warner
nodes.description: Oversees the intelligence community; FISA reauthorization due April 2026.

nodes.name: House Intelligence
nodes.description: House side of intelligence oversight.

nodes.name: Senate Foreign Relations
nodes.description: Treaties, ambassadors, arms sales notifications.

nodes.name: Government Accountability Office
nodes.dm: Comptroller General (acting) after Gene Dodaro's retirement
nodes.description: Audits and impoundment rulings; findings against the executive largely ignored in 2025.

nodes.name: Congressional Budget Office
nodes.description: Its scores shape what can pass under budget rules.

nodes.name: Supreme Court
nodes.dm: Chief Justice John Roberts; Thomas, Alito, Sotomayor, Kagan, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, Barrett, Jackson
nodes.description: Final word on the Constitution and federal law. Since 2024 it has expanded presidential immunity and removal power (Trump v. United States; the Humphrey's Executor line), curbed nationwide injunctions (Trump v. CASA) and ended Chevron deference (Loper Bright).

nodes.name: U.S. Courts of Appeals
nodes.description: Decide ~50,000 appeals a year; the effective last word in most cases.

nodes.name: U.S. District Courts
nodes.description: Trial courts; issued hundreds of orders against 2025 executive actions, many later narrowed on appeal.

nodes.name: Judicial Conference & Administrative Office
nodes.dm: Presided over by the Chief Justice
nodes.description: Judiciary's own governance, budget requests, ethics rules.

nodes.name: FISA Court
nodes.dm: 11 district judges designated by the Chief Justice
nodes.description: Approves foreign-intelligence surveillance in secret.

nodes.name: U.S. Sentencing Commission
nodes.description: Writes the guidelines that anchor federal sentences.

nodes.name: State courts
nodes.dm: 50 state supreme courts (38 states elect judges); ~30,000 judges
nodes.description: Handle 95% of all cases; state supreme courts increasingly decide abortion, redistricting and election disputes.

nodes.name: American Bar Association
nodes.description: Accredits law schools and writes model ethics rules; stripped of its judicial-vetting role.

nodes.name: Big Law firms
nodes.dm: Kirkland & Ellis, Latham, Skadden, Paul Weiss and peers; managing partners
nodes.description: Litigation capacity for hire. Several firms signed pro-bono deals with the White House in 2025 after punitive executive orders; others sued and won.

nodes.name: State governments
nodes.dm: 50 governors (27 R / 23 D) and legislatures; National Governors Association
nodes.description: Police power, elections, education, Medicaid, the National Guard. The main counterweight to a unified federal government, and the main instrument for enforcing its agenda in aligned states.

nodes.name: State attorneys general
nodes.description: Sue the federal government, big tech and pharma; enforce consumer and antitrust law.

nodes.name: Local governments
nodes.dm: ~90,000 units: mayors, county boards, councils; U.S. Conference of Mayors, NLC
nodes.description: Zoning, policing, property tax, permits — the level of government that most shapes daily life.

nodes.name: State & local police
nodes.dm: ~18,000 agencies, ~700k sworn officers; chiefs appointed by mayors/councils
nodes.description: The everyday face of state force; ~7M arrests a year.

nodes.name: County sheriffs
nodes.dm: ~3,000 elected sheriffs; run most county jails
nodes.description: Independently elected law enforcement; key partners for ICE via 287(g) agreements.

nodes.name: National Guard
nodes.dm: ~430k troops; commanded by governors unless federalized (Title 10) or under Title 32 request
nodes.description: Deployed to Los Angeles, Washington, Memphis, Chicago and Portland in 2025 over some governors' objections; litigation over federalization ongoing.

nodes.name: District attorneys & state prosecutors
nodes.description: Charging discretion over the vast majority of criminal cases.

nodes.name: Election officials & secretaries of state
nodes.dm: ~10,000 local election offices; 50 chief election officers
nodes.description: Run registration, counting and certification; under pressure from DOJ voter-roll demands and the 2025 elections executive order.

nodes.name: School boards
nodes.description: Curriculum, budgets and superintendents for 49M students.

nodes.name: State utility & insurance regulators
nodes.dm: Public utility commissions; insurance commissioners (11 elected)
nodes.description: Set electricity rates and decide whether insurers can raise premiums or leave a state.

nodes.name: Public pension funds
nodes.dm: CalPERS, CalSTRS, NY Common, Texas TRS, Florida SBA; ~$6T combined
nodes.description: Among the largest allocators to private equity, hedge funds and index managers; boards appointed by states.

nodes.name: Republican Party
nodes.dm: RNC Chair Joe Gruters; effective leader: President Trump
nodes.description: Controls the White House, both chambers and a majority of statehouses; fully aligned with the president.

nodes.name: Democratic Party
nodes.dm: DNC Chair Ken Martin; congressional leaders Schumer and Jeffries
nodes.description: Out of federal power; leverage through states, courts, filibuster and the 2026 midterms.

nodes.name: Super PACs & dark-money networks
nodes.dm: MAGA Inc., Senate Leadership Fund, Congressional Leadership Fund, Fairshake, Future Forward, America PAC
nodes.description: Unlimited spending vehicles enabled by Citizens United; ~$4B+ per cycle.

nodes.name: K Street lobbying industry
nodes.dm: ~13,000 registered lobbyists; ~$4.5B/yr disclosed; Brownstein, Akin, Holland & Knight, Ballard Partners
nodes.description: Revolving door between government and the firms that pay for access.

nodes.name: Billionaire donor class
nodes.dm: ~900 U.S. billionaires; top 1% of donors supply most super PAC money
nodes.description: Individuals whose checks can fund a Senate race outright; also endow universities, think tanks and media.

nodes.name: Heritage Foundation
nodes.description: Project 2025 personnel and policy pipeline into the administration.

nodes.name: Federalist Society network
nodes.dm: Leonard Leo (co-chair; Marble Freedom Trust); Eugene Meyer
nodes.description: Shaped a majority of the federal bench; relationship with the White House cooled in 2025.

nodes.name: Think tanks (AEI, Brookings, Cato, CAP, CSIS)
nodes.description: Manufacture the policy options and the experts who fill agencies.

nodes.name: AIPAC
nodes.dm: CEO Elliot Brandt; United Democracy Project PAC
nodes.description: Bipartisan pressure on foreign policy; spends heavily in primaries.

nodes.name: NRA
nodes.description: Diminished by scandal but still the organizing brand for gun-rights voters.

nodes.name: AARP
nodes.description: Guardian of Social Security and Medicare politics.

nodes.name: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
nodes.description: Largest lobbying spender in most years; litigates against regulation.
nodes.aliases: US Chamber of Commerce|Chamber of Commerce of the USA

nodes.name: Business Roundtable
nodes.description: CEO-level lobbying on tax and trade.

nodes.name: ALEC
nodes.description: Model legislation copied across state legislatures.

nodes.name: Koch network (Stand Together, AFP)
nodes.dm: Charles Koch; Koch Industries (~$125B revenue, private)
nodes.description: Libertarian-conservative funding and grassroots machine.

nodes.name: American Petroleum Institute
nodes.description: Oil and gas trade association; drafted much of the 2025 deregulatory wish list.

nodes.name: American Farm Bureau Federation
nodes.description: Farm-state political muscle behind the farm bill.

nodes.name: AFL-CIO
nodes.dm: President Liz Shuler; ~15M members across 63 unions
nodes.description: Labor federation; Democratic turnout machine.

nodes.name: Teamsters
nodes.description: UPS, freight and warehouse leverage; politically bipartisan since 2024.

nodes.name: SEIU
nodes.description: Health-care, janitorial and public-sector workers; rejoined AFL-CIO 2025.

nodes.name: UAW
nodes.description: Auto strikes; supportive of tariffs on imported vehicles.

nodes.name: Teachers' unions (NEA, AFT)
nodes.dm: NEA President Becky Pringle; AFT President Randi Weingarten; ~4.7M members
nodes.description: Largest union in the country; dominant in school-board and state politics.

nodes.name: Police unions (FOP, PBAs)
nodes.description: Contracts, discipline appeals and endorsements that few mayors defy.

nodes.name: Hollywood unions (SAG-AFTRA, WGA, DGA, IATSE)
nodes.dm: SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin; WGA; DGA; IATSE
nodes.description: Strike power over studios and streamers; AI terms are the live issue.

nodes.name: Players' associations (NFLPA, NBPA, MLBPA)
nodes.description: Collective bargaining with leagues; revenue splits and lockout leverage.

nodes.name: Elon Musk
nodes.dm: Richest person in the world; controls Tesla, SpaceX, X/xAI
nodes.description: Largest single political donor of 2024; ran DOGE in early 2025, broke with the president mid-2025, later partially reconciled. Owns critical launch and communications infrastructure the government depends on.

nodes.name: Larry Ellison
nodes.dm: Oracle chairman/CTO; father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison
nodes.description: Financed the Paramount takeover and the Warner Bros. Discovery bid; Oracle anchors the TikTok U.S. joint venture.

nodes.name: Jeff Bezos
nodes.dm: Amazon executive chair (~9%); owner of The Washington Post; Blue Origin
nodes.description: Reshaped the Post's opinion pages in 2025; Blue Origin competes for NASA and defense launch.

nodes.name: Peter Thiel
nodes.description: Patron of JD Vance and of the defense-tech ecosystem (Palantir, Anduril).

nodes.name: Murdoch family
nodes.description: Controls Fox Corp and News Corp through the family trust.

nodes.name: Soros network (Open Society)
nodes.description: Progressive funding for civil society, prosecutors' races and Democratic super PACs; target of 2025 investigations.

nodes.name: Miriam Adelson
nodes.dm: Las Vegas Sands controlling shareholder; Preserve America PAC

nodes.name: BlackRock
nodes.description: Top-3 shareholder of most large U.S. companies through index funds; votes proxies, manages pension and government money.

nodes.name: Vanguard
nodes.dm: CEO Salim Ramji; ~$11T AUM; owned by its funds

nodes.name: State Street

nodes.name: JPMorgan Chase

nodes.name: Goldman Sachs
nodes.description: Investment banking and the alumni pipeline into Treasury and the Fed.

nodes.name: Bank of America
nodes.description: ~70M consumer clients.

nodes.name: Citigroup
nodes.description: Global transaction banking; dollar plumbing.

nodes.name: Morgan Stanley
nodes.description: Wealth management and capital markets.

nodes.name: Wells Fargo
nodes.dm: CEO Charlie Scharf; asset cap lifted 2025

nodes.name: Berkshire Hathaway
nodes.dm: CEO Greg Abel (since Jan 2026); Chairman Warren Buffett
nodes.description: Owns BNSF railroad, GEICO, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and large stakes in Apple and banks; ~$350B cash.

nodes.name: Private equity (Blackstone, KKR, Apollo, Carlyle)
nodes.dm: Stephen Schwarzman; Marc Rowan; Joseph Bae & Scott Nuttall; Harvey Schwartz
nodes.description: Own hospitals, nursing homes, rental housing, local news, insurers; ~$4T dry powder plus 401(k) access opened by 2025 EO.

nodes.name: Hedge funds (Citadel, Bridgewater, Millennium, Elliott)
nodes.dm: Ken Griffin; Paul Singer; Izzy Englander; Nir Bar Dea
nodes.description: Activist campaigns, Treasury-market plumbing, and outsized political donations.

nodes.name: Payment networks (Visa, Mastercard)
nodes.dm: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney; Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach
nodes.description: Toll collectors on ~$10T of card spending; can cut off merchants.

nodes.name: Exchanges (NYSE/ICE, Nasdaq, CME)
nodes.dm: Jeff Sprecher; Adena Friedman; Terry Duffy
nodes.description: Listing rules and market structure.

nodes.name: Credit rating agencies (Moody's, S&P, Fitch)
nodes.dm: Rob Fauber; Martina Cheung; Paul Taylor

nodes.name: Big Four accounting (Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG)
nodes.description: Audit sign-off on nearly every public company; tax-policy lobbying.

nodes.name: Management consultants (McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Booz Allen)
nodes.dm: Bob Sternfels; Christoph Schweizer; Christophe De Vusser; Horacio Rozanski
nodes.description: Sell the same playbook to agencies, hospitals and corporations; $65B in federal consulting contracts targeted for cuts in 2025.

nodes.name: Crypto industry
nodes.dm: Coinbase (Brian Armstrong), Circle, Tether, a16z crypto; Fairshake PAC
nodes.description: Won the GENIUS Act (stablecoins) in 2025; a market-structure bill and friendly SEC followed. Ties to the president's own ventures (World Liberty Financial).

nodes.name: Apple
nodes.description: iPhone platform gatekeeper for ~60% of U.S. smartphones; App Store rules govern developers and creators.

nodes.name: Microsoft
nodes.description: Enterprise software, Azure, ~27% of OpenAI's for-profit, Xbox/Activision, major federal cloud vendor.

nodes.name: Alphabet (Google, YouTube)
nodes.description: Search, YouTube and Android decide what most Americans see. Found to be an illegal monopolist (2024–25); remedies limited by the court.

nodes.description: Billions in loans and guarantees to Boeing, nuclear, minerals and allied projects; DFC expanded to $200B+ authority in 2025.

nodes.name: Bureau of Indian Affairs & Interior trust duties

nodes.name: Tribal nations (574 federally recognized)

nodes.description: Sovereigns with treaty rights, ~$40B gaming industry, senior water rights on the Colorado and Missouri, and votes that swing AZ, MT, NV, WI.

nodes.name: Bureau of Reclamation (western water)
nodes.description: Operates Hoover, Glen Canyon and the Central Valley Project. Post-2026 Colorado River operating rules decide which cities and farms get cut.

nodes.name: BOEM & BSEE (offshore oil, gas and wind)
nodes.description: Lease sales in the Gulf and Alaska; offshore-wind permits paused or revoked in 2025 (Empire Wind, Revolution Wind) — a permit is a kill switch.

nodes.name: NIST & CAISI (standards, AI evaluation)
nodes.dm: NIST Director; Center for AI Standards and Innovation
nodes.description: Sets the technical standards agencies and contractors must meet: cybersecurity framework, AI risk framework, cryptography, election-machine testing.

nodes.name: NTIA (spectrum & broadband)
nodes.description: Runs the $42B BEAD broadband program (rewritten in 2025 toward satellite), manages federal spectrum, and advises the President on internet policy.

nodes.name: Commerce trade enforcement (Section 232, antidumping)
nodes.dm: Secretary Howard Lutnick; International Trade Administration
nodes.description: Section 232 "national-security" tariffs on steel, autos, copper, chips and pharma are Commerce's lever and survive even if IEEPA tariffs fall in court.

nodes.name: National laboratories (Los Alamos, Livermore, Sandia, Oak Ridge, Argonne)
nodes.dm: Run by contractors (Triad, UC, Battelle, Honeywell) under DOE/NNSA
nodes.description: Nuclear-weapons design, supercomputing, fusion and grid research; ~$25B a year and the scientific workforce agencies rely on.

nodes.name: NHTSA (auto safety, fuel economy)
nodes.description: Recalls, crash investigations (Tesla Autopilot/FSD), robotaxi exemptions, and CAFE standards — penalties for which were zeroed out in 2025.

nodes.name: DOT modal regulators (FMCSA, FRA, PHMSA, FTA)
nodes.dm: Administrators appointed by the President under Secretary Sean Duffy
nodes.description: Trucking hours, rail safety and crew size, pipeline safety, transit grants — and the English-proficiency crackdown on truckers in 2025.

nodes.name: OSTP & the AI/crypto czar
nodes.dm: Director Michael Kratsios; David Sacks (AI & crypto czar)
nodes.description: Writes the AI Action Plan, pushes federal preemption of state AI laws, and brokers between the labs, chipmakers and the White House.

nodes.name: Inspectors General

nodes.description: Hears appeals from fired federal workers; "Schedule Policy/Career" reclassification and RIFs strip protections for tens of thousands.

nodes.name: Agency adjudication & administrative law judges

nodes.name: Combatant commands (NORTHCOM, CYBERCOM, SOCOM)

nodes.name: DARPA & defense R&D
nodes.description: ~$4B a year seeding the technologies (internet, GPS, drones, mRNA) that later define industries; picks winners among labs and startups.

nodes.name: Library of Congress & Copyright Office

nodes.name: D.C. Circuit

nodes.description: Reviews most federal agency actions and D.C. district orders — removal cases, tariffs, deportations, spending. Feeder court to the Supreme Court.

nodes.name: Court of International Trade & Federal Circuit

nodes.description: Exclusive jurisdiction over tariff challenges (the IEEPA cases began here) and patent appeals that decide pharma and tech monopolies.

nodes.name: Bankruptcy courts

nodes.description: Decide who gets paid when firms fail — Purdue, Steward Health, Rite Aid, X Corp. creditors. Private equity and hedge funds live here.

nodes.name: Budget committees & reconciliation

nodes.description: Reconciliation lets 51 senators rewrite taxes, Medicaid, SNAP and student loans (OBBBA, July 2025) — the most powerful lawmaking path left.

nodes.name: Senate Parliamentarian
nodes.description: Rules what can ride in a reconciliation bill (Byrd rule). Unelected, overrulable only by the presiding officer — which leadership has declined to do.

nodes.name: Senate HELP Committee

nodes.name: Senate Commerce & House Transportation

nodes.description: Farm bill, SNAP (cut in OBBBA), crop insurance, CFTC jurisdiction over crypto — the intersection of food, money and rural votes.
